topic: Filtering criteria for visitor session data
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on refining the logic used to identify valid, non-zero duration sessions and determine if a user is 'permanent' in a given location. Initial concerns were raised about multiple zero-duration sessions across different locations or time periods.

[me] proposed an improved filtering condition using SQL syntax: `HAVING sum(session_duration) >= 3600*2 OR uniqExact(facility_num) > 3`. This logic requires either a total session duration of at least two hours, or the user must have visited more than three unique facilities.

This proposed criteria was accepted as a better method to prevent filtering out legitimate foot traffic (e.g., people passing by an entrance daily). The requirement for visiting multiple unique facilities (`uniqExact(facility_num) > 3`) was confirmed as essential.
decisions: Adopt the filter condition: `HAVING sum(session_duration) >= 3600*2 OR uniqExact(facility_num) > 3` to define valid sessions.
